verses.gurmukhi: ਜੈਸੇ ਜਲ ਕੂਪ ਨਿਕਸਤ ਜਤਨ ਕੀਏ ਸੀਚੀਅਤ ਖੇਤ ਏਕੈ ਪਹੁਚਤ ਨ ਆਨ ਕਉ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaise jal koop nikasat jatan ke'ee seecheeat khet ekai pahuchat na aan kau ||

en.bdb: Just as water from a well can be drawn by different methods, such as bucket and rope, Persian wheel etc. and then it is directed to irrigate a field and it goes nowhere else.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਥਿਕ ਪਪੀਹਾ ਪਿਆਸੇ ਆਸ ਲਗਿ ਢਿਗ ਬੈਠਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਨੁ ਭਾਂਜਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਕਤ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਕਉ ॥
verses.translit_en: pathik papeehaa piaase aas lag ddig baiTh bin gun bhaa(n)jan tirapat kat praan kau ||

en.bdb: A traveller and a rain-bird may keep on sitting thirsty near a well but cannot quench their thirst without means to draw water from the well and therefore cannot assuage their thirst.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤੈਸੇ ਹੀ ਸਕਲ ਦੇਵ ਟੇਵ ਸੈ ਟਰਤ ਨਾਹਿ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਏ ਦੇਤ ਫਲ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਸਮਾਨ ਕਉ ॥
verses.translit_en: taise hee sakal dhev Tev sai Tarat naeh sevaa ke'ee dhet fal kaamanaa samaan kau ||

en.bdb: Likewise, all gods and goddesses can do something within their power. They can reward a devotee for his services only to that extent and that too of worldly desires.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰਨ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗੁਰ ਬਰਖਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਹਿਤਿ ਬਰਖ ਹਰਖਿ ਦੇਤ ਸਰਬ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਕਉ ॥੪੫੧॥
verses.translit_en: pooran braham gur barakhaa a(n)mirat hit barakh harakh dhet sarab nidhaan kau ||451||

en.bdb: The service of gods and goddesses is trivial in benefits whereas that of True Guru blesses one with Naam which is the treasure-house of all the virtues and spiritual happiness. (451)
